title: Matcher
description: The matcher interface: contributed shape operators, plan actions, variant dimensions, comparability and generators. Matching and generating are one interface because a generator's output must be admitted by the shape it generates for (shape spec §3.4), and one declared authority is what lets the engine check that pair. See spec.md §7.

Compile.title: Compile
Compile.description: Turn one shape node carrying this component's operator into a plan fragment. A contributed operator is compiled and executed exactly as a core one is; nothing about it is special-cased in the interpreter (plan grammar §4.6).

node.description: The shape node, owned by design 2.2.

fragment.description: A plan fragment in design 2.4's grammar. A fragment that uses only core actions needs no apply at all — the cheapest kind of component operator, and fully visible in explain (spec.md §7.1).

Apply.title: Apply
Apply.description: Execute one of this component's actions against values. Batched from day one: spike 1.4 measured 1.4 microseconds per pipe call, fine per value at test scale and the obvious lever if it ever is not (spec.md §7.2).

config.description: The action's configuration, as the compiled plan node carries it.

values.description: The values to apply the action to. One entry unless the component declared the 'batch-apply' capability.

results.description: One result per input value, in the same order. Each is a plan result document in design 2.4's result form, so a component mismatch is a mismatch and not a special case.

dimensions.description: Dimensions this operator contributes, as design 2.2's variant-space documents. Point order is minimal-to-maximal — that ordering is the declaration variant semantics §3.1 asks a component facet for. Gates must form a forest; an engine rejects a set that does not (spec.md §7.4). Empty is the common case.

Compare.title: Compare
Compare.description: The containment procedure a subsumption checker calls for an operator declared 'exact' (shape spec §8, spec.md §7.5).

verdict.description: Whether admits(provider) is contained in admits(consumer). 'unknown' is a first-class answer; a component MUST answer it rather than guess, because a wrong 'yes' is how a checker loses its users.

context.description: What the generator is allowed to know — the variant assignment, values already produced in this interaction. Open vocabulary. Ambient state (a clock, randomness) comes from the component's own runtime under its grants, not from here.

MatchValue.title: MatchValue
MatchValue.description: One value in the shape language's model, wrapped the same way a slot value is so that octets and text are unambiguous.

path.description: Where this value came from, for attributing a result.

PlanResult.title: PlanResult
PlanResult.description: Design 2.4's Result document, unchanged: status ('ok', 'value', 'error'), the value or the message and path. Deliberately not restated here — a component mismatch is a mismatch in the plan grammar's own result form, and two definitions of it would eventually disagree. The worked examples are validated against design 2.4's schema to prove the two agree.
